title: Stable Enough to Go Home

patient.name: Mdm Rahimah binte Osman
patient.presenting_complaint: Back in the day ward after right eye cataract surgery; asking when she can go home

history.hpc: Mdm Rahimah has returned to the day ward after uneventful right eye cataract surgery under local anaesthesia. She says: 'Operation finish already, can go home now or not?' She feels well, mild scratchy sensation in the eye, no severe pain or nausea. The OT must monitor her recovery, record vital signs, and confirm she is stable before discharge.
medications: Post-op antibiotic and steroid eye drops (right eye, to start as directed)
history.social_hx: Lives with son who will take her home. Fasted pre-op, now able to take light refreshment.

examination_findings.anterior_segment: Right eye shield in place; no excessive pain or discharge reported

investigations.dayward_postop_care: Post-operative monitoring documented: blood pressure (BP), respiratory rate (RR), and pulse rate (PR) recorded and stable. Patient comfortable, no severe pain, bleeding, or nausea. TCU (next follow-up appointment time/date) documented. Post-op medications (eye drops) recorded with instructions. Patient observed until stable for discharge.
investigations.vital_signs: BP, RR, PR within acceptable ranges and stable on repeat.
investigations.comfort: Mild scratchiness only; no red-flag symptoms.

diagnosis: Uncomplicated recovery after day-case cataract surgery: stable vital signs, comfortable patient, and completed discharge documentation (TCU and post-op medications). The OT competency is correct post-op monitoring, recognising when a patient is stable for discharge, and clear documentation; clinical decisions remain the nurse's/doctor's.

immediate: Monitor and record vital signs (BP, RR, PR) and check for pain, bleeding, or nausea
Confirm the patient is comfortable and observe until stable for discharge
Document the TCU (time and date of next follow-up appointment)
Record the post-op medications prescribed and explain how/when to use them
Ensure a responsible person will accompany her home
Escalate to the nurse/doctor if any vital sign is abnormal or red-flag symptoms appear
follow_up: Attend the TCU appointment for the post-op review
Use the prescribed eye drops as directed and keep the shield as advised
Return urgently if increasing pain, redness, discharge, or vision drop occurs
patient_education: Explain she can go home once her observations are stable and she is comfortable
Teach the eye drop schedule and shield use, and to avoid rubbing the eye
Give the warning signs (increasing pain, redness, discharge, vision loss) and when to return
Confirm her son will take her home and remind her of the follow-up date

key_points: Confirms the surgery done and the operated eye
Checks for post-op red-flag symptoms (severe pain, nausea, bleeding)
Acknowledges the patient's question about discharge
Records BP, RR, and PR and confirms they are stable
Assesses comfort and checks for complications
Documents the TCU and post-op medications
Observes the patient until stable for discharge
Recognises stable vitals and comfort as criteria for safe discharge
Distinguishes normal early recovery from red-flag complications
Knows abnormal vitals/symptoms must be escalated, not discharged
Knows clinical discharge decisions rest with the nurse/doctor
Documents vitals, TCU, and post-op medications clearly
Provides clear drop/shield instructions and warning signs
Escalates appropriately if any concern arises
